haiku-low.q1: When the caller's transaction commits its pending row in the monolith notifications table. If the caller rolls back, no row exists.
haiku-low.q2: It redelivers the message after 30 seconds, possibly to a different consumer.
haiku-low.q3: Five attempts, waiting 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes between them. After attempt 5 the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q4: shipping_update, then order_confirmed, then password_reset, one at a time behind a flag. Before password_reset: staging fault tests pass, order_confirmed held 3 days, p99 under 60s.
haiku-low.q5: The notification's id, passed as idempotency_key. It comes from the row. Within 24 hours MailRelay drops a repeat and returns success, same as a new accept.
haiku-low.q6: A monolith relay claims rows, commits owner=service, then publishes to the notification topic. Done when the broker confirms and published_at is set.
haiku-low.q7: Routing flag notifications.route.<type>, read at claim time. Unowned rows go to whichever side claims them; owned rows finish with their owner.
haiku-low.q8: Insert with ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING ignores the second copy. Sends also use id as the key, so MailRelay drops repeats.
haiku-low.q9: Only after committing the row as queued, before any send. If it crashes before the ack, the message is redelivered and the insert does nothing.
haiku-low.q10: In the service's own notifications table, in attempts and next_attempt_at columns. The service's polling claim loop, every 5 seconds, acts on it.
haiku-low.q11: They are not moved or re-sent. They stay owned by the service and drain there, and the relay keeps running. The monolith cannot take them back.
haiku-low.q12: id, type, email, payload, created_at, schema_version, attempts and first_attempt_at. Subject and body are rendered by the service from its own template copy.

sonnet.q1: At enqueue (step 1): business code's enqueue_notification(tx, ...) inserts a pending row (owner NULL, 0 attempts) into the monolith notifications table. The row exists only if the caller's own transaction commits; if it rolls back, no row exists and nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: The broker is at-least-once: a message not acknowledged within 30 seconds is redelivered, possibly to a different consumer.
sonnet.q3: 5 attempts total, with waits of 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes before attempts 2 to 5 (about 15 minutes of retries). After attempt 5 the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q4: Order: shipping_update, then order_confirmed, then password_reset, via the routing flag. Staging rehearsal/fault injection must pass before the first move. shipping_update holds at least 3 days. order_confirmed then holds 3 days. Before password_reset moves, steps 8 and 9 must have passed, meaning the p99 enqueue-to-MailRelay latency gate (under 60 s on order_confirmed, service-owned rows only) passed. A staging rollback drill is also run before the production move.
sonnet.q5: The notification's id, passed as idempotency_key. It comes from the notification row's id (the monolith notifications table id). If MailRelay already accepted a send with that key in the last 24 hours, it drops the repeat and returns success, which looks the same to the caller as a new accept.
sonnet.q6: The monolith relay claims owner-NULL rows of service-routed types, sets owner to service and commits, then publishes the row to the notification topic on the broker. When the broker confirms, the relay sets published_at. The service ingests it. The monolith's part is done at that point, though its row stays pending until the service's status event (sent or failed) arrives on the status topic and the status consumer updates the row.
sonnet.q7: The monolith decides, using the routing flag notifications.route.<type> (monolith or service), read with flags.get at the moment a row with owner NULL is claimed. The claimer then records its choice in the owner column. Rows already having an owner finish with that owner.
sonnet.q8: Service ingest inserts with ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING, so the duplicate insert does nothing and the message is acked; only one row exists to send. Also every send uses id as the MailRelay idempotency key.
sonnet.q9: The service acks only after the insert commits (before sending, which happens later via the polling claim loop). If it crashes after commit but before ack, the message is redelivered and the insert does nothing.
sonnet.q10: In the service's own database notifications table (attempts, next_attempt_at, lease_until, first_attempt_at, status). The service's 5-second polling claim loop acts on it, claiming queued rows that are due or sending rows with expired leases.
sonnet.q11: Nothing moves. Flipping the flag back to monolith takes effect within about a minute (about 15 s per the failure table). Rows already owned by the service are not moved or re-sent. They drain on the service, and the monolith relay keeps running (publishing unpublished service-owned rows) until no unpublished owner='service' rows remain. The service can't be scaled to zero until no owner='service' rows are queued or sending. The monolith cannot take them back; if the service is broken they wait or are failed and paged by the 20-hour guard (open question).
sonnet.q12: Per notification: {id, type, email, payload, created_at, schema_version, attempts, first_attempt_at} (created_at substituted for first_attempt_at in the legacy case). The email content (subject and body) is produced in the service, rendered from its own copy of the templates, with golden tests ensuring byte-identical output to the monolith.
